4.28 Noise Considerations. No significant noise potential can be linked to the operation of a hydropower facility. There are no problems envisioned in this case as no bothersome noise levels are expected to be produced.
4.29 Hazardous Materials. No unusual potentially dangerous or hazardous meterials are expected to be used or stored at the damsite. The various units do contain oil which must be filtered from time to time to maintain its insulative properties. Other petroleum products will also be maintained at the site but should not present any unusual threat to the environment when handled properly. Spills are possible but would probably be contained within the confines of the structure.
4.30 Land Features and Uses. Hydroelectric releases are expected to initially increase the rate of bank sloughing in isolated areas, particularly where steep exposed banks exist. This will result from the greater fluctuation of flow levels in the river channel, but after the proposed operation has been in progress for a few weeks these effects will become similar to the effects of the present operational procedures.
4.31 Vegetative Resource. Riparian vegetation along the Rio Grande will be slightly impacted by the initial increase in the rate of bank sloughing.
4.32 Esthetics. Hydroelectric releases could be accompanied by a noticeable odor (hydrogen sulfide) during the months when the reservoir is stratified and hypolimnial discharges enter the tailrace. The powerhouse will have little visual effect because it will be below the dam and visible only from directly downstream. In addition, in this perspective, it will blend into the background of the dam structure. The switchyard, which will be located above the powerhouse, will also be immediately downstream of the dam and restricted to most viewers. It should not detract from the natural surroundings, especially observing the Rio Grande from the dam itself.
4.33 Recreation. The effects of the proposed project operation should have minimal effect on recreation. On Amistad Reservoir, recreation should slightly benefit from a gradually drawn down versus abrupt drop in lake levels as presently exists. Falcon Reservoir should also benefit from a more stable water level. Recreational endeavors on the Rio Grande should benefit from a more continuous flow. However, restricted access on the Rio Grande by property owners will continue to limit recreation opportunities.
4.34 Wildlife Resource. The primary impact on wildlife should be the loss of habitat resulting from initial bank sloughing along the Rio Grande. Since riverbanks should stabilize soon after establishment of a new release pattern, the effect on adjacent wildlife forms should not be major. There will be no adverse effects on any known rare or endangered wildlife.
4.35 Rio Grande Fishery. Project operation will probably have the most pronounced effect on river fisheries in the reach of the Rio Grande from the dam to Del Rio. No data exist to accurately define water quality conditions below the dam during hydropower releases, which will be the primary cause of impact on river fisheries. Of special concern relative to the aquatic environment is the possible extreme case which could occur during the later months of the thermal stratification period. During this time, approximately July through November, near zero or zero oxygen conditions can develop in the lower level of the reservoir. Hydropower releases during these periods may therefore significantly lower temperatures and dissolved oxygen and may also elevate concentrations of toxic materials such as ammonia-nitrogen and hydrogen sulfide below the dam.
